places.name: African Burying Ground Memorial Park
places.summary: A memorial on the spot where thirteen African people were buried in the 1700s. Their remains were found under a city street, and DNA testing confirmed their origins. It is the only African burial ground of its time in New England confirmed this way.
places.why_go: A city paved over its own history, then dug it up and had to answer for it. The memorial is built for people to gather, not only to look.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Gora's interest in history that was hidden, and for Stivka's reflective side. A short and serious start to the trip.

hours.note: Confirm interior access close to travel.

places.address: African Burying Ground Memorial Park, Chestnut Street, Portsmouth, New Hampshire

places.name: USS Albacore: The Teardrop-Hull Experiment
places.summary: A research submarine from 1953 with a rounded teardrop shape. It was never a fighting boat. It was built to test speed underwater, and its shape became the model for every modern submarine.
places.why_go: You climb inside a very small experimental submarine that changed how all later ones were built. A test machine, not a war story.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Gora's engineering interest and Stivka's love of technical stories. The tight space makes it memorable for everyone.

hours.note: Open daily through Indigenous Peoples' Day.

places.address: USS Albacore Museum, 600 Market Street, Portsmouth, New Hampshire

places.name: Nubble Light from Sohier Park
places.summary: A working lighthouse with a red roof, standing on a small rock island just off the shore. You see it from the granite and grass of the park opposite.
places.why_go: The first big coast picture of the trip: a lighthouse on its own rock with waves all around it. You cannot go onto the island, and we say so up front.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's first strong sea photo and for Paco's easy group stop. Nobody has to walk far.

hours.note: Sohier Park is open year-round; no parking 01:00-05:00.

places.address: Sohier Park, Nubble Road, York, Maine

places.name: The Woodman Museum
places.summary: Four old buildings holding stuffed animals, minerals, local art, the home of an anti-slavery senator, and a fortified house from 1675. Nothing has been modernized.
places.why_go: An old-fashioned museum of curiosities, still arranged the way museums used to be. Strange, wide-ranging and a little dusty.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's love of odd places and for Gora's interest in how museums once showed the world.

hours.note: April-November Wednesday-Sunday; reconfirm 2026 fall hours.

places.replacement_reason: Replace Albacore when the group prefers a messier natural-history and local-history cabinet with more personality.
places.address: Woodman Museum, 182 Central Avenue, Dover, New Hampshire

replacement.reason: Replace Albacore when the group prefers a messier natural-history and local-history cabinet with more personality.

route_variant.routing_note: OSRM road-network baseline with no live traffic; use the same live-traffic gate as the scheduled day.

places.name: Victoria Mansion: Technology in a Gilded Interior
places.summary: An Italian-style villa from 1860 that survives almost complete: painted walls, gas lights, indoor plumbing and furniture, all designed together as one scheme.
places.why_go: Not simply a rich house. Almost nothing was changed, so you see how the whole thing was meant to work, down to the pipes and the lamps.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's decorated interiors and for Gora's interest in the systems inside a building.

hours.note: Open daily May 1-October 31; last admission before close.

places.address: Victoria Mansion, 109 Danforth Street, Portland, Maine

places.name: Portland Head Light & Fort Williams
places.summary: The oldest working lighthouse in the United States, standing above the surf beside gun batteries and the ruins of an old coastal fort.
places.why_go: A famous lighthouse, a rough sea and a hidden military site in one walk, instead of three separate stops.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's landmark photo and for Gora's interest in the defenses under a pretty view.

hours.note: Park is broader-access; lighthouse museum is daily through October 31.

cost.note: Small museum admission; parking is separate.

places.address: Portland Head Light, 1000 Shore Road, Cape Elizabeth, Maine

places.name: Eastern Promenade Blue-Hour Walk
places.summary: A grassy hillside park above Casco Bay, laid out under the influence of the landscape designer Frederick Law Olmsted. Ferries and islands fill the water below.
places.why_go: Fresh air and harbor light before the first social night. No ticket and no fixed time.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's evening light and for Stivka's calm hour before a loud one.

hours.note: Confirm interior access close to travel.

places.address: Eastern Promenade, Portland, Maine

places.name: Arcadia Pinball & Local-Tap Night
places.summary: An adults-only bar full of pinball machines, arcade cabinets and board games, with local beer. It is a games bar, not a nightclub.
places.why_go: Competition makes people talk. Everyone can join in, and everyone can leave before it gets tiring.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Paco's group energy and for Gora's social side. Viki and Stivka can play or just watch.

hours.note: Open Monday; closed Tuesday.

cost.note: Drinks and game spend are excluded from the route budget.

places.address: Arcadia, 504 Congress Street, Portland, Maine

places.name: Desert of Maine
places.summary: A field of bare glacial sand that slowly buried a farm, its soil and its buildings. There are trails, and some of the old structures are still visible.
places.why_go: A desert in the middle of coastal Maine. It looks impossible, and it happened because of how the land was farmed.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's strange landscape photos and for Gora's interest in a mistake people made with the land.

hours.note: Open daily.

places.replacement_reason: Replace Victoria Mansion when sunshine makes the glacial landscape more magical than another preserved interior.
places.address: Desert of Maine, 95 Desert Road, Freeport, Maine

replacement.reason: Replace Victoria Mansion when sunshine makes the glacial landscape more magical than another preserved interior.

route_variant.routing_note: OSRM road-network baseline with no live traffic; use the same live-traffic gate as the scheduled day.

places.name: Guardians of the Seeds at Coastal Maine Botanical Gardens
places.summary: Five enormous wooden trolls by the Danish artist Thomas Dambo are hidden around a large seaside botanical garden. Each is built from reclaimed wood and linked to a different part of a tree.
places.why_go: Finding five giant hidden trolls turns a garden walk into a hunt. Their size is genuinely surprising when you reach them.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's best photos of the trip and for Paco's group activity. Everyone joins the search.

hours.note: Regular season continues through October 18.

cost.note: Adult online admission; advance purchase is cheaper than walk-up.

places.address: Coastal Maine Botanical Gardens, 105 Botanical Gardens Drive, Boothbay, Maine

places.name: Maine State Prison Showroom
places.summary: A shop selling furniture, model ships, carved boxes and other objects made by people held in Maine's prisons.
places.why_go: The work is highly skilled, and buying it opens a real conversation about prison labor and craft. Nobody is put on display.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Gora's interest in work and justice, and for Stivka's thinking about dignity. Viki finds the carving beautiful.

hours.note: Open seven days.

places.address: Maine State Prison Showroom, 358 Main Street, Thomaston, Maine

places.name: Rockland Breakwater Lighthouse Walk
places.summary: A lighthouse at the end of a granite wall from the 1890s that runs almost a mile out into Penobscot Bay. You walk out along the stone to reach it.
places.why_go: A mile of granite straight out to sea, with a lighthouse at the end. One of the best sunset pictures of the whole trip.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's sunset photo and for Gora's quiet walk. The stones need care, but the walk is flat and short.

hours.note: Breakwater is exposed and uneven; skip for rain, high wind or slippery stone.

places.address: Rockland Breakwater Lighthouse, Rockland, Maine

places.name: Maine Maritime Museum & Percy and Small Shipyard
places.summary: A 20-acre former shipyard. A full-size steel outline stands where a six-masted wooden schooner was built, showing its real shape and size. The museum also tells the story of the people who built such ships.
places.why_go: The steel outline shows you the real size of a wooden ship. It works in rain, costs less and needs less walking than the gardens.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Gora's interest in building things at scale and for Viki's shipyard structures.

hours.note: Open daily.

places.replacement_reason: Replace the troll gardens for bad weather, garden fatigue or a stronger appetite for ships and labor history.
places.address: Maine Maritime Museum, 243 Washington Street, Bath, Maine

replacement.reason: Replace the troll gardens for bad weather, garden fatigue or a stronger appetite for ships and labor history.

route_variant.routing_note: OSRM road-network baseline with no live traffic; use the same live-traffic gate as the scheduled day.

places.name: Owls Head Transportation Museum
places.summary: More than 150 old cars, motorcycles, bicycles and aircraft, kept in working order rather than parked as decoration.
places.why_go: These machines still run. You see how transport actually developed, not a row of polished show cars.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Gora's love of mechanical history. The early aircraft shapes and bright paintwork surprise Viki too.

hours.note: Open daily year-round.

places.address: Owls Head Transportation Museum, 117 Museum Street, Owls Head, Maine

places.name: Fort Knox & Penobscot Narrows Observatory
places.summary: A granite coastal fort, and beside it a bridge tower with a lift rising to a public viewing floor 420 feet above the river.
places.why_go: Dark stone passages underground, then a lift to a view over the whole valley. Two completely different experiences on one ticket.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Gora's military engineering and for Viki's autumn view from high above the river.

hours.note: Observatory October hours; fort grounds remain open later.

cost.note: Nonresident combined adult admission; reconfirm 2026 fee.

places.address: Penobscot Narrows Bridge Observatory, Prospect, Maine

places.name: Bar Harbor Shore Path at Blue Hour
places.summary: A flat path along Frenchman Bay, past granite edges, large old hotels and the Porcupine Islands offshore.
places.why_go: An easy walk with a strong run of views, and no extra drive or ticket after arriving at Acadia.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's blue-hour photos and for everyone's need to stretch after the drive.

hours.note: Confirm interior access close to travel.

places.address: Bar Harbor Shore Path, Bar Harbor, Maine

places.name: Penobscot Marine Museum's Sea-Captain Village
places.summary: A group of sea captains houses, with boats, navigation instruments and objects brought home from around the world. This small town once had an unusual number of deep-sea captains.
places.why_go: One small town sent captains all over the world. This is that story at human scale, not another big machine collection.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Gora's interest in trade and travel, and for Stivka's family and community stories.

hours.note: Tuesday-Sunday through the third weekend of October.

places.replacement_reason: Replace Owls Head when the group prefers domestic architecture and seafarer lives over vehicles.
places.address: Penobscot Marine Museum, 2 Church Street, Searsport, Maine

replacement.reason: Replace Owls Head when the group prefers domestic architecture and seafarer lives over vehicles.

route_variant.routing_note: OSRM road-network baseline with no live traffic; use the same live-traffic gate as the scheduled day.

places.name: Cadillac Mountain Sunrise
places.summary: A granite summit with views over islands and open ocean. On these October dates it is the first place in the United States to catch the sunrise.
places.why_go: The first sunrise in the country, and you drive most of the way up. This is the early start the whole trip is built around.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's biggest photo and for Paco's shared group moment. No long walk is needed.

hours.note: Cadillac vehicle reservation is required May 20-October 25, 2026.

cost.note: Vehicle reservation and park pass divided across four; car count can change this.

places.address: Cadillac Mountain Summit, Acadia National Park, Maine

places.name: Ocean Path: Sand Beach to Thunder Hole Sampler
places.summary: A section of coastal path over pink granite, past spruce trees and open ledges, ending at Thunder Hole where waves boom into a narrow inlet.
places.why_go: The classic Acadia coast, kept to about three easy miles, with a car waiting at the end if anyone has had enough.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's coastal photos and for Gora's walk. The car exit protects everyone's energy.

hours.note: Use the safer roadside path; wet granite and heavy surf can cancel the walk.

places.address: Thunder Hole, Park Loop Road, Acadia National Park, Maine

places.name: Jordan Pond & the Bubbles View
places.summary: A clear glacial lake with the two rounded hills called the Bubbles at the far end. We walk only the near shore, not the full loop.
places.why_go: The calmest, most balanced view in Acadia, right after the exposed coast. Short and restful.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's reflections and Stivka's quiet moment. Nobody has to do the whole loop.

hours.note: Confirm interior access close to travel.

places.address: Jordan Pond House, Acadia National Park, Maine

places.name: International Cryptozoology Museum—New Bangor Home
places.summary: The only museum in the world devoted to cryptozoology, the search for animals that may not exist. It holds real zoological specimens, claimed evidence, and the pop culture of Bigfoot and sea serpents.
places.why_go: Enjoy the strange claims, then judge the evidence separately. That split is exactly the point of the visit.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Gora's interest in what counts as proof, and for Viki's love of odd museums.

hours.note: Open year-round seven days at 490 Broadway; the former Portland sites are closed.

places.address: International Cryptozoology Museum, 490 Broadway, Bangor, Maine

places.name: Stephen King's House—Public-Road Exterior
places.summary: A deep red Victorian house behind an iron gate decorated with bats and spiders. It is now used as a writers' archive, not a house you can enter.
places.why_go: The gate alone is worth the stop, and it ties these streets to the Maine in his books. We look from the public road and nothing more.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Stivka's and Gora's interest in his books. Viki gets the gate. Twenty minutes and no trespassing.

hours.note: Confirm interior access close to travel.

places.address: Stephen King House, 47 West Broadway, Bangor, Maine

places.name: Thomas Hill Standpipe at Sunset
places.summary: A huge riveted iron water tank hidden inside a wooden shingled tower 110 feet high, standing on a hill above the city.
places.why_go: A giant piece of Victorian city engineering, disguised as a wooden tower. Even with the stairs closed, the hill finishes the afternoon well.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Gora's interest in city infrastructure and for Viki's sunset view over Bangor.

hours.note: Interior tours are rare special events and are not promised.

places.address: Thomas Hill Standpipe, 41 Thomas Hill Road, Bangor, Maine

places.name: Seal Cove Auto Museum
places.summary: A quiet collection of brightly restored cars, motorcycles and early motoring design, from about 1895 to the 1920s.
places.why_go: A precise wet-weather swap: still mechanical and colorful, but from a narrower period than Owls Head, so it does not repeat it.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Gora's mechanical detail and for Viki's colors and shapes. Quiet and indoors.

hours.note: Open daily May 1-October 31.

places.replacement_reason: Replace the Acadia sunrise-and-walk block for hard rain, dangerous wind or total exhaustion; keep Jordan Pond only if conditions improve.
places.address: Seal Cove Auto Museum, 1414 Tremont Road, Seal Cove, Maine

replacement.reason: Replace the Acadia sunrise-and-walk block for hard rain, dangerous wind or total exhaustion; keep Jordan Pond only if conditions improve.

places.name: Cole Land Transportation Museum
places.summary: Old trucks, snowplows, railway equipment and military vehicles, showing how people and goods moved across difficult Maine country.
places.why_go: The best parts are the ordinary working machines and the personal stories of the people who drove them, not glamorous cars.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Gora's interest in real working machines, and for Stivka's interest in service and memory.

hours.note: Open daily May 1-November 11.

places.address: Cole Land Transportation Museum, 405 Perry Road, Bangor, Maine

places.name: Maine Mineral & Gem Museum: Hold the Moon
places.summary: Maine tourmaline and local mining history sit beside about 6,000 rocks from space, including pieces of the Moon, Mars and the asteroid belt.
places.why_go: A small mountain town holds rock from other worlds, and some of it you can meet at hand level. The size of the collection is the shock.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Gora's love of real science and for Viki's photos of stone and light. Stivka gets genuine wonder.

hours.note: Open Friday; final admission 16:00.

places.address: Maine Mineral and Gem Museum, 99 Main Street, Bethel, Maine

places.name: Bethel Common & Mountain-Town Evening
places.summary: A small 18th-century village green with mountains behind it and a short walkable center.
places.why_go: A deliberately quiet night: dinner, conversation and rest between two museum-heavy days.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Paco's management of the group's energy and for Stivka's calm evening.

hours.note: Confirm interior access close to travel.

places.address: Bethel Common, Bethel, Maine

places.name: Colby College Museum of Art
places.summary: A large free collection of American art and modern installations, on a small college campus far from any big city.
places.why_go: Serious art for free, in a shorter visit, before the long drive to Bethel.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's art photos and for Stivka's calm gallery time. Paco likes that it costs nothing.

hours.note: Reconfirm fall Friday hours before promotion.

places.replacement_reason: Replace Cole when the group is vehicle-museum saturated or wants a free contemporary-art reset.
places.address: Colby College Museum of Art, 5600 Mayflower Hill Drive, Waterville, Maine

replacement.reason: Replace Cole when the group is vehicle-museum saturated or wants a free contemporary-art reset.

places.name: Weeks State Park: Summit House & Fire Tower
places.summary: A 1.6-mile road climbs Mount Prospect to a stone fire tower and a restored country estate from 1912. From the top you see from the Presidential Range across to Vermont's Green Mountains.
places.why_go: You drive to the summit and get a full circle of view at the height of the autumn color. The 2026 season runs to 12 October, so our date works.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's widest autumn photo and for Gora's interest in fire towers. No hard climbing.

hours.note: On Saturday October 10 the auto road is open 10:00-17:00, tower to 16:30 and house museum to 16:00.

places.address: Weeks State Park, 200 Weeks State Park Road, Lancaster, New Hampshire

places.name: Fall for St. J Foliage Train
places.summary: A 45-minute ride in historic carriages along the Passumpsic and Connecticut rivers, run during St Johnsbury's autumn festival on these exact dates.
places.why_go: Autumn color from a train instead of a car window, and the ticket also gets us into the planetarium for free.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Paco's shared experience and for Viki's photos from the window. Everyone sits down for an hour.

hours.note: October 10-11, 2026 is confirmed; exact departures and ticket release are pending.

places.address: St. Johnsbury Welcome Center, 51 Depot Square, St Johnsbury, Vermont

places.name: Fairbanks Museum's Victorian Cabinet
places.summary: A Victorian hall in heavy Romanesque style, still full of mounted animals, weather instruments and thousands of specimens, arranged as they were in the 1800s.
places.why_go: It feels like walking into one collector's mind rather than a modern science center. The train ticket also covers the planetarium.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Gora's interest in how knowledge was collected, and for Viki's untouched period interior.

hours.note: Open daily; festival scavenger hunt runs all weekend.

cost.note: Adult museum admission; planetarium is free with festival train ticket.

places.address: Fairbanks Museum and Planetarium, 1302 Main Street, St Johnsbury, Vermont

places.name: Dog Mountain & the Dog Chapel
places.summary: The hilltop folk-art world of the artist Stephen Huneck. At its center is a small chapel whose walls are covered with thousands of handwritten notes about dogs people have loved and lost.
places.why_go: Funny and heartbreaking in the same hour. Of all our backup stops, this is the one most likely to become the real memory of the day.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Stivka's feeling for memory and loss, and for Viki's folk art. Nobody leaves unaffected.

hours.note: Gallery and chapel hours; grounds dawn to dusk.

places.replacement_reason: Replace the train and Fairbanks when train tickets fail, museum fatigue is high or the group wants folk art with real emotional weight.
places.address: Dog Mountain, 143 Parks Road, St Johnsbury, Vermont

replacement.reason: Replace the train and Fairbanks when train tickets fail, museum fatigue is high or the group wants folk art with real emotional weight.

places.name: Sunday at Dormition Greek Orthodox Church
places.summary: A living Orthodox parish holding Orthros and the Divine Liturgy. We attend the service. This is not a tour of the building.
places.why_go: Sunday stays a real Sunday, and the group starts the day with something shared.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Stivka above all, and for the whole group as common ground. We follow the parish and stay for the whole Liturgy if we can.

hours.note: Orthros 09:00; Divine Liturgy approximately 10:00. Reconfirm parish calendar.

places.address: Dormition of the Mother of God Greek Orthodox Church, 600 South Willard Street, Burlington, Vermont

places.name: Shelburne Museum: The Three-Hour Treasure Hunt
places.summary: Thirty-nine buildings holding folk art, mechanical figures, a round barn, Impressionist paintings, circus carvings, and the 220-foot steamboat Ticonderoga, which sits on dry land.
places.why_go: Too big to see fully, so each person picks one thing to chase and we all meet at the steamboat. Everyone gets their own discovery.
places.best_fit_note: Good for all four in different ways. Paco gets a plan that lets people split up without losing the group.

hours.note: Open daily May 9-October 25, including Indigenous Peoples' Day.

places.address: Shelburne Museum, 6000 Shelburne Road, Shelburne, Vermont

places.name: Burlington Waterfront & Church Street
places.summary: Sunset over Lake Champlain, then the pedestrian shopping street of Church Street, with its brick fronts and easy places to eat.
places.why_go: City energy without a tight schedule, and with two cars we can come and go freely before the music.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's browsing and Paco's flexible evening. Everyone eats what they want.

hours.note: Confirm interior access close to travel.

places.address: Waterfront Park, Burlington, Vermont

places.name: Radio Bean Calendar-Gated Music Night
places.summary: A small neighborhood venue that puts on several live sets a night across different styles. The room is small enough to feel social.
places.why_go: The second optional big night, and only if the line-up is rock, heavy, folk or genuinely strange. We do not go just to tick a box.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Stivka's music and Gora's social side. Viki gets a real local room rather than a tourist bar.

hours.note: Promote only after the October 11 lineup and age policy are published.

cost.note: Cover and drinks excluded from the route budget.

places.address: Radio Bean, 8 North Winooski Avenue, Burlington, Vermont

places.name: Museum of Everyday Life: Deep Seated
places.summary: An unheated barn museum with no staff. You turn on the lights yourself and look at ordinary objects taken seriously. The 2026 exhibition is about chairs.
places.why_go: Nobody is there. You let yourself in, switch on the light, and think about chairs. It feels like finding something left unlocked on purpose.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's love of the genuinely strange and for Gora's interest in ordinary things. Free, and unlike anywhere else.

hours.note: Open daily, self-service; the space is unheated, so bring a coat.

places.replacement_reason: Replace Shelburne Museum when the group wants one truly eccentric exhibition instead of a vast canonical collection; this variant uses almost the entire drive cap.
places.address: Museum of Everyday Life, 3482 Dry Pond Road, Glover, Vermont

replacement.reason: Replace Shelburne Museum when the group wants one truly eccentric exhibition instead of a vast canonical collection; this variant uses almost the entire drive cap.

places.name: Ben & Jerry's Flavor Graveyard—No Fake Factory Tour
places.summary: Granite gravestones with real written epitaphs for discontinued ice cream flavors, on a hill above the factory. There is a shop and a viewing platform over the production floor.
places.why_go: A cemetery for dead ice cream flavors, written completely seriously. Note clearly: guided tours are closed 9-12 October, so we are not promising one.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Paco's group humor and Viki's photos. Nobody should expect a factory tour on our dates.

hours.note: No guided tours October 9-12; mezzanine public viewing, scoop shop and seasonal grounds remain.

cost.note: No tour ticket planned; ice cream is personal food spend.

places.address: Ben and Jerry's Factory, 1281 Waterbury-Stowe Road, Waterbury, Vermont

places.name: Hope Cemetery: Barre's Granite Autobiography
places.summary: Immigrant granite carvers made their own cemetery into a field of sculpture: airplanes, racing cars, soccer balls, a double bed, and portraits cut from local stone.
places.why_go: The carvers chose their own memorials, so the stones show pride in their craft, migration, and the lung disease that killed many of them.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Gora's labor history and Viki's eye for sculpture. For everyone, it is a burial ground first and an attraction second.

hours.note: Public visiting hours; yield completely to funerals.

places.address: Hope Cemetery, 201 Maple Avenue, Barre, Vermont

places.name: Plymouth Notch: The Night a Farmhouse Became the White House
places.summary: A village kept almost unchanged, where Calvin Coolidge's father swore him in as president by lamplight after Harding died during the night.
places.why_go: A president took the oath in his father's farmhouse by lamp light. The whole village is still there: church, shop, cheese factory, barns and graves.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Gora's political history and Stivka's interest in duty. Viki gets a complete old village.

hours.note: Official season is late May to mid-October; confirm October 12 is inside the final 2026 operating week.

places.address: President Calvin Coolidge State Historic Site, 3780 Vermont Route 100A, Plymouth Notch, Vermont

places.name: VINS Raptor Center & Forest Canopy
places.summary: A center for rescued birds of prey, with live programs and a raised walkway that takes you from ground level up into the tree canopy.
places.why_go: Live eagles and owls, and a walk through the treetops. It works in rain and needs no real hiking.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's bird close-ups and Stivka's gentle side. Gora gets the science of rehabilitation.

hours.note: Open daily.

places.replacement_reason: Replace Plymouth Notch if its seasonal buildings are closed, or when the group needs living nature after two history-heavy days.
places.address: VINS Nature Center, 149 Natures Way, Quechee, Vermont

replacement.reason: Replace Plymouth Notch if its seasonal buildings are closed, or when the group needs living nature after two history-heavy days.

route_variant.routing_note: OSRM road-network baseline with no live traffic; use the same live-traffic gate as the scheduled day.

places.name: Quechee Gorge from the Reopened Bridge
places.summary: The Ottauquechee River has cut a deep narrow channel below a road bridge. You look straight down into it, with autumn color on both walls.
places.why_go: Thirty-five minutes for a real piece of landscape, with no walking, before two museums and the drive to Manchester.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's gorge photo and Gora's quick nature break. Easy for everyone.

hours.note: Use signed pedestrian routes and any current bridge safety controls.

places.address: Quechee Gorge Bridge, Quechee, Vermont

places.name: American Precision Museum in the 1846 Armory
places.summary: Inside the old Robbins & Lawrence Armory from 1846, belt-driven machine tools show how America learned to make identical, interchangeable parts.
places.why_go: This is where mass production actually began, and the machines are still here to inspect. It also covers what that did to the people who worked them.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Gora's engineering interest and Viki's old machine shop. The building itself is part of the story.

hours.note: Open daily May 1-October 31.

places.address: American Precision Museum, 196 Main Street, Windsor, Vermont

places.name: Saint-Gaudens Sculpture Grounds—Tuesday Exterior Edition
places.summary: The estate of the sculptor Augustus Saint-Gaudens, with bronze figures, formal gardens, studios and views across to Mount Ascutney.
places.why_go: Sculpture set in a designed landscape. Be clear: on Tuesday the visitor center, galleries and house interiors are closed, so we walk the grounds.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's sculpture and garden photos and Stivka's calm hour. We plan for the grounds only.

hours.note: Grounds are open in daylight; seasonal buildings operate Thursday-Monday and are closed Tuesday.

places.address: Saint-Gaudens National Historical Park, 139 Saint Gaudens Road, Cornish, New Hampshire

places.name: Path of Life Sculpture Garden
places.summary: Eighteen outdoor artworks follow birth, ambition, sorrow, forgiveness, death and rebirth, across open fields, a stone labyrinth and a maze of hemlock trees.
places.why_go: A walk through a whole life told in sculpture. Four people will read the same symbols completely differently, which is the point.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Stivka's reflective side and Viki's landscape art. A quiet alternative to another machine collection.

places.name: Frank Lloyd Wright's Zimmerman & Kalil Houses
places.summary: A two-hour guided visit to two houses by Frank Lloyd Wright. One is a small Usonian home; the other is one of only seven Usonian Automatic houses, built from modular blocks. Both keep their original furniture.
places.why_go: Two neighbors gave the same architect the same ideas and got completely different houses. You feel it in the light and the ceiling heights.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's architecture and Gora's interest in how a system becomes a home. Booking is required.

hours.note: 2026 season runs April 22-December 27; tours Wednesday-Sunday at 09:30, 12:00 and 14:30.

cost.note: Confirm exact 2026 combined-house public tour price; museum admission is included.

places.address: Currier Museum of Art, 150 Ash Street, Manchester, New Hampshire

places.name: Currier Museum Highlights
places.summary: A compact regional art museum, running from European painting to American decorative arts and modern New England work.
places.why_go: Entry is already included with the Wright house tour, so one focused hour adds real value without risking the drive back to Boston.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Viki's and Stivka's gallery hour. Paco likes that it costs nothing extra.

hours.note: Open Wednesday-Sunday.

cost.note: Included with the Wright houses tour.

places.name: SEE Science Center & LEGO Millyard
places.summary: Hands-on science experiments around an enormous LEGO model of Manchester's Amoskeag Millyard as it looked at its industrial peak.
places.why_go: Cheap, hands-on and easy to leave early. The LEGO city also links the play to the real mills outside.
places.best_fit_note: Good for Paco's last-day mood and Viki's curiosity. Gora gets the real industrial history behind the model.
